recoveryObjectives: Predeclared operator-state and database RPO: 5 minutes each. Operator-state-only loss RTO: 15 minutes with the database available. Database or combined-loss RTO: 30 minutes through application-service restoration, including manual work and verification. Procedure and timing boundaries: support/qualification/0.2.0.md.
runEvidence: Release transaction 38699615146 from d1859174 (tag v0.2.4), published by run 39215485952 and re-verified from the tag by 39214596338. Manifest-backed acceptance matrix on the release's own digests: amd64 CI 39184792094 (harness ef9f68ba, no runtime change from the source) and arm64 CI 38714365984, 54 of 54 cells and every declared scenario in its phase window. Installation from the published guide: 39216106322 (fresh on amd64), 39216111992 (fresh on arm64), 39216109320 (over v0.2.3 on amd64), 39216114555 (over v0.2.3 on arm64). Demonstration on the release digests: 38714370026. Capacity, recovery and the evidence bundles: see PA-07, PA-08 and PA-12.

PA-01.evidence: Release manifest sha256:ebf96e065a21a5c70a5e68bfba8029581ac31db124640f14ef8227e66b144916 names every digest above; the coverage table below is the 54-cell matrix CI 39184792094 (linux/amd64) and 38714365984 (linux/arm64) ran on those digests, attempt 1, with each job ID and log hash in functional/<arch>/coverage-audit.json of the public bundle.

PA-02.evidence: Every approval-binding and drift refusal refused with zero unauthorized statements received by the database server, each with a positive control, and each fresh approval executed, on both engines and families in all 54 cells of CI 39184792094 and 38714365984 (data-plane, schema-approvals, schema-faults, migration-authority and both migration suites).

PA-03.evidence: Faults before Job creation, after dispatch, during SQL, after SQL before persistence and during lock release, with process, leader and node loss, deletion, suspension and changed bindings, showed no overlap or replay in all 54 cells of CI 39184792094 and 38714365984; the three capacity soaks repeated an all-manager restart burst on both engines without a lost or replayed operation.

PA-04.evidence: Functional refusal, retry and hung-result rows passed in CI 39184792094 and 38714365984. Each of the three capacity soaks converged after cold start, every churn round, the registry outage, the all-manager replacement and the 30-second database delay within their frozen targets; overload at 40 resources recovered after returning to 20 within 5 minutes (amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 2m32s, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 2m25s, arm64 1.37 MySQL 1m47s).

PA-05.evidence: Boundary-value API cases, the installed RBAC and admission identities, the documented reader Roles, credential scans and the egress example enforced by the CNI passed in CI 39184792094 and 38714365984. Every capacity lab ran restricted Pod Security, the frozen ResourceQuota and the kindnet NetworkPolicy build, checked by the lab preflight.

PA-06.evidence: Install, upgrade, late-failure recovery, rollback refusal, uninstall, reinstall over retained CRDs and the quota- and Pod Security-constrained exported-chart install passed on 1.35, 1.36 and 1.37 on both architectures. The published guide installed v0.2.4 fresh and as an upgrade over the published v0.2.3 on both architectures: 39216106322 (fresh on amd64), 39216111992 (fresh on arm64), 39216109320 (over v0.2.3 on amd64), 39216114555 (over v0.2.3 on arm64).

PA-07.evidence: Nine recovery cells passed on published v0.2.2 with 698 assertions, each within its objectives (RTO 130 to 592 seconds against 900 or 1800, database RPO under 60 seconds). The applicability chain carries them to d1859174: the runtime changes since are the result-cleanup deletion budget (#655), the refresh slots (#661) and the chart version, which change when expired results are removed and when a read-only refresh starts, not the restore procedures, stored formats or recovery decisions. Records: recovery/ in the public bundle.

PA-08.evidence: Soak, backlog and overload passed every driver check at the support window's edges: 1.35 PostgreSQL on amd64 and arm64, 1.37 MySQL on arm64. Exact manager API demand from Metadata audit on all three API servers, complete for every manager process, peaks inside the measured windows at amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 6,735, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 6,483, arm64 1.37 MySQL 6,627 for the soaks and amd64 1.35 PostgreSQL 5,890, arm64 1.35 PostgreSQL 6,161, arm64 1.37 MySQL 5,839 for the backlogs, requests per 60 seconds against 7,000. Overload is outside the profile and judged by refusal, safety and recovery. 0.2.3 exceeded the budget once on the MySQL soak (7,236); #661 spaces the refresh cycles of a fleet sharing an interval. A burst after measurement during API-server restarts is follow-up #657.

PA-09.evidence: Every alert row fired and resolved at the receiver within its frozen target, with ordinary approval waits kept from paging, in the lifecycle, alerting-operations and certificates cells of CI 39184792094 and 38714365984.

PA-10.evidence: The published guide ran verbatim on fresh clusters for PostgreSQL and MySQL on both architectures, including the shipped kubectl-ptah reading the plan: 39216106322 (fresh on amd64), 39216111992 (fresh on arm64), 39216109320 (over v0.2.3 on amd64), 39216114555 (over v0.2.3 on arm64). All demonstration scenarios ran on the release digests (38714370026). The four signed kubectl-ptah assets read a real applied plan, schema and migration on measured capacity labs: darwin-amd64 (Darwin amd64 through Rosetta on Apple Silicon on the Docker host), darwin-arm64 (native Darwin arm64 on the Docker host), linux-amd64 (native Linux amd64), linux-arm64 (native Linux arm64).

PA-11.evidence: All eight published assets are byte-identical to the qualified draft; checksums, attestations naming d1859174 and the anonymous cosign signature verified after publication. The report-only scan of every shipped image and binary reached nothing in source; the executor findings remain follow-up #610.

PA-12.evidence: Public bundle: https://github.com/stokaro/ptah-operator/releases/tag/qualification-0.2.4, an immutable release whose assets were downloaded anonymously and matched their checksums. Restricted bundle: 13 age-encrypted archives on the evidence host, each read back, decrypted with the retained identity and refused to an unprivileged user (custody records under custody/ in the public bundle). This record and its decision are in the public bundle and at support/acceptance/0.2.0.json in the repository.

handoff.recoveryAccess: Restricted archives decrypt with the retained age identity held by Ptah Engineering; access to the evidence host is limited to its owner account.
handoff.reassessmentTriggers: Changes to shipped bytes, declared scope, installation authority or network settings, workload or retention limits, recovery objectives, or a relevant security finding require an applicability review and reruns of the affected evidence.
handoff.deploymentChecks: Before enabling autonomous Apply, install by the verified digests with the recorded values; verify admission, RBAC and network controls, monitoring-to-receiver delivery, backup access and one representative approved database change.
handoff.automaticOperationPolicy: Ptah Engineering enables autonomous operation only after the deployment checks, recovery access and the stated policy boundaries are verified; an unresolved Apply keeps the documented manual recovery path.
